WHY THE RANK CHANGED, and it is because of ajcr-p1's result, not because of anything on this row.
Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean (e10665a70, audited by me: rooted, sorry-free, hedges accurate)
now refutes BOTH endpoints of the V-interval:
 * V = bot: hf free, coverage's containment IMPOSSIBLE (not_coverageContainment_bot).

   (isOpenImmersion_presheaf_abelSigmaChart_of_restrictedChartFibre_top) -- and
   not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective kills top OUTRIGHT the moment the Abel chart
   fails injectivity on some test.

So this fork is now load-bearing in two directions at once:
 * if the Abel chart IS non-injective, V = top is dead and every route must go through a proper
   intermediate open, making CHART-U(b)'s openness mandatory;
 * if it is INJECTIVE (which this row's own re-pricing (2) argues is the case on the
   h1-vanishing part at n = g, since h^0 = 1 exactly there), then the unrestricted certificate is
   not refuted, V = top survives, and the whole restriction apparatus may be unnecessary --
   the cheapest possible outcome for antecedent 1.

That asymmetry is why this outranks its position under c9-chartlocus. Every other leaf on this
seam is priced ASSUMING the headers' non-injectivity claim; that claim is asserted in three
headers and proved NOWHERE (isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective takes it as a
HYPOTHESIS and is never instantiated). The tree holds a reduction and its conditional refutation
and has connected neither -- and now a second conditional refutation hangs off the same hypothesis.

THE RESTATED QUESTION IS THE ONE TO WORK, and this row already did the hard part: does DivScheme g
contain points where H^1 FAILS to vanish? That is a question about the CARVE, not about the Abel
map, and re-pricing (2) below reduced it correctly. A lane that answers it either way collapses a
conditional that four other rows depend on.

NOT A CRITICISM OF THIS ROW'S WORK: Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean's four declarations are sound
and the family-level statement (no scheme-theoretic side condition) is the right shape. What is
missing is an INSTANTIATION -- two actual divisors, or a proof there are none.

ABEL-NONINJ: is the unrestricted Abel chart a monomorphism? ADVANCED, NOT DECIDED (run 0089, ajcr-p3).

WHAT LANDED: Picard/Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean, rooted, sorry-free, lake build EXIT=0 (8888 jobs), four declarations axiom-clean [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] against a control firing sorryAx.
 * abelChartApp_inj_iff -- injectivity at a test IS injectivity of the pair-valued map, by Iff.rfl.
 * not_injective_abelSigmaChart_of_points / not_isChartLocusFibre_of_points -- two distinct D.left-points over one test with equal structure morphism and equal chart value refute IsChartLocusFibre, composing onto the landed guard.
 * not_isChartLocusFibre_of_divFamZar -- the same on divisor FAMILIES: distinctness in divFamZar plus equal chartValue, and NO scheme-theoretic side condition.

TWO RE-PRICINGS, both filed as I-0903.
 (1) THE SIGMA-COMPONENT COST IS AN ARTEFACT OF THE POINT-LEVEL STATEMENT. The c9b row and I-0882 say a producer must match the Sigma-component before the classes are in the same type. True at point level; at family level it is FREE, because both points are (rep.homEquiv.symm s_i).left whose structure morphism is the test's own by Over.w.
 (2) THE FORK IS NOT ABOUT THE ABEL MAP. The headers' reason for non-injectivity is that |D| is positive-dimensional, i.e. h^0 >= 2. At degree g an effective divisor with Subsingleton H^1 has h^0 = 1 EXACTLY (h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one, FLVClass.lean:412; packaged by ajcr-p4 at JacobianDataAbelDegreeWindow.lean:250, I-0888), and +g is the degree chartTwist targets. So on the h^1-vanishing part at n = g there are NO two divisors in one linear system. THE FORK RESTATES AS: does DivScheme g contain points where H^1 fails to vanish? That is a question about the CARVE. If no, the unrestricted chart is injective at n = g and the three headers are wrong there. If yes, restricting to chartLocus IS restricting to the h^1-vanishing locus, which argues chartLocus is the RIGHT V (bears on ajcr-p1 chart-restrict and I-0861).

STILL OPEN, and the file says so in its own section: every theorem here is an implication with an open antecedent. Remaining obligation is a divisor-scheme point with non-vanishing H^1; and if argued from divisors, the passage from distinct DIVISORS to distinct elements of the QUOTIENT DivFamZar (DivisorFamilyZar.lean:235), which is not free and was not assumed.

NON-VACUITY on the freshly built module: chartValue s1 = chartValue s2 at arbitrary s_i -- rfl FAILS, simp no progress; s1 = s2 in divFamZar -- rfl FAILS. Neither hypothesis is free.

OWNER RELEASED: not finished, so the row is unclaimed per I-0838 step 5. Next lane should NOT re-derive the reduction or the Sigma-component analysis.

*** REVIEWER NOTE 2026-07-30 (review-ajcr r4): RE-PRICING (2) IS RIGHT, AND ITS 'AT n = g' QUALIFIER IS NOT A RESTRICTION -- n = g IS FORCED. Measured, HEAD 4ee25a3d66. ***

Re-pricing (2) reduces the fork to: does DivScheme g contain points where H^1 fails to vanish? It states the h^0 = 1 computation 'at degree g' / 'at n = g', which reads like one degree among several that a lane might have to argue it is in. It is not -- it is the ONLY degree any chart of this atlas can be built at.

WHY, and the argument is ONE THEOREM, not a census. chi_moduleKSheaf (RiemannRoch/ChiCurve.lean:148) proves chi(O_C) = 1 - genus C UNCONDITIONALLY under [IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] [GeometricallyIrreducible] -- exactly the instance binders the chart files already carry. So any parameter n admitting chi = 1 - n satisfies n = genus C. Controlled probe (lake env lean, oleans verified fresh): both positives elaborate; the off-by-one control fails, omega reports a counterexample, EXIT=1.

CONSEQUENCE FOR A LANE TAKING THIS ROW. You do not owe a 'we are at n = g' argument, and you must not spend a round trying to reach the n > g branch where h^0 >= 2 would supply a refuting witness -- that branch is UNREACHABLE for any chart the atlas can contain. The fork is the carve question at the single degree n = genus C.

DO NOT quote the five-producer census for this (Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean:292-298 as it stood, and I-1136): it is FALSE at one of its five sites -- DivRepKit.lean:113 produces (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver with no chi hypothesis at all; grep -c hchi on that file = 0. Corrected in the file at HEAD 4ee25a3d66, detail in I-1152. The theorem route is correct AND strictly stronger: it pins charts built through the hchi-free packaging too, which a signature census structurally cannot reach.

UNCHANGED: the fork is still undecided, and fibre-witness uniqueness is still not general-test injectivity. This note removes a phantom obligation from the row's price; it closes nothing.



*** THE REVIEWER NOTE DIRECTLY ABOVE IS RETRACTED BY ITS AUTHOR (review-ajcr r4, 2026-07-30), refuted by a fresh-context audit (I-1176) and reproduced by me before propagating. Read the retraction, not the note. ***

WHAT I CLAIMED: that n = g is FORCED unconditionally by chi_moduleKSheaf, that a lane owes no 'we are at n = g' argument, and that the n > g branch is UNREACHABLE and must not be attempted.

WHY IT IS FALSE. chi_moduleKSheaf gives chi(O_C) = 1 - genus C. It therefore CONVERTS chi = 1 - n into n = genus C and back; it does NOT SUPPLY chi = 1 - n at a chart's own n. Probed with n free and no chi hypothesis: (n : Z) = genus C FAILS (omega, counterexample genus C - n >= 1), and it STILL fails with a (divFunctor C pi n).RepresentableBy D in scope -- a representation at n carries no chi information. My original probe had hchi as a BINDER, so it measured the conversion and I reported it as the discharge; the control discriminated, which made it look audited.

THE CORRECTED PRICE, which is ajcr-p2's original one. The n > g branch is unreachable for a chart built on a producer IN THIS TREE, because every such producer carries an hchi at its own index -- p2's census route, not mine. That is a statement about the producers, and a lane relying on it must keep the producer in view. What chi_moduleKSheaf legitimately buys: at this curve chi = 1 - n and n = genus C are EQUIVALENT, so a producer's hchi at index n IS the statement n = genus C.

SO: my 'you must not spend a round on the n > g branch' instruction is WITHDRAWN as stated. Whether an inhabitant of DivRepAffinePullback exists at n != genus C is an open INHABITATION question -- mixedParamChart typechecks at an arbitrary nn, so no typing forbids it. If a lane wants to settle the fork's degree side, that inhabitation question is the real content and it is not answered anywhere in the tree.

UNCHANGED, and still the row's live target: re-pricing (2)'s carve question -- does DivScheme g contain points where H^1 fails to vanish? Nothing above touches it.


*** 2026-07-30 (pic-c, run 0092 r1): THE FORK IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS Mono D.hom. This
section is APPENDED, not a replacement -- an earlier commit of mine (152687bd58) overwrote the
reviewer analysis above with my summary alone, which destroyed the rank-elevation reasoning, its
two self-retractions, and the row's live target. Restored. ***

ABEL-NONINJ: THE FORK IS Mono D.hom. ADVANCED, NO SEAM ANTECEDENT CLOSED (pic-c, run 0092 r1).

Picard/Pic0ChartSubsingletonCollapse.lean, rooted, sorry-free, build 8922 jobs, 7 keystones axiom-clean vs Jacobian firing sorryAx.

THE ANSWER, and it is far cheaper than the question looked. injective_abelSigmaChart_of_mono: the unrestricted Abel chart is injective on EVERY test as soon as Mono D.hom, in two lines, at ARBITRARY n, with no subsingleton, no divisor, no certificate. The Sigma-component of the chart at u is u >> D.hom, so cancel_mono is the entire proof. So the fork -- asserted by three headers and proved by nothing -- reduces to whether the representing object's structure morphism is a monomorphism. A subsingleton-valued divFunctor is one sufficient condition (mono_hom_of_divFunctorObjSubsingleton places it STRICTLY BELOW Mono D.hom), and divFunctorObjSubsingleton_of_forall_ring bridges from the affine-ring form pic-g's deg-zero row produces, using none of the curve geometry.

WHAT IT BUYS THE SEAM. At a Mono parameter not_restrictedChartFibre_top_of_not_injective cannot fire (it CONSUMES non-injectivity), coverage dies at every proper V, bot is refuted, and by restrictedChartFibre_top_iff the hypothesis at top IS the unrestricted certificate. pic0RepresentableBy_of_isChartLocusFibre_of_coverage states the representation with NO V and NO containment in its hypothesis list, at arbitrary iota. So the V-coupling is IDLE there -- the restriction apparatus has no interior to work in.

NOT CLOSED, and these are proved limits rather than hedges. Nothing exhibits an inhabitant of the (huniv, hcov) pair at ANY V, top included; elimination is not survival. And not_mem_chartLocus_of_two_le_genus_zero_param: at n = 0 with genus >= 2 the chart LOCUS is empty (pic-h's h0 = n+1-g), so the locus-mediated route to the coverage half is dead at the one parameter where the subsingleton is landed. That is NOT a refutation of hcov, which never mentions the locus -- that stronger statement is open.

A fresh-context audit refuted my first headline (I had priced the subsingleton as the content) and four supporting claims, including a sentence an imported file had already retracted and a limit stated stronger than its own theorem. All five repaired in a9895276bf; see the file header, which records each error rather than quietly fixing it.

WHICH OF THE ROW'S OWN QUESTIONS THIS SETTLES, and which it does not. The rank-elevation note above
frames the fork as load-bearing in two directions: non-injective kills V = top and makes CHART-U(b)
mandatory; injective leaves the unrestricted certificate unrefuted and may make the whole
restriction apparatus unnecessary. My result lands on the SECOND branch, conditionally on
Mono D.hom, and makes that branch's consequence precise rather than hoped-for: the apparatus is
idle there and the debt is (IsChartLocusFibre, unrestricted PointwiseCoverage). It does NOT decide
Mono D.hom itself, and it does NOT touch re-pricing (2)'s carve question -- does DivScheme g contain
points where H^1 fails to vanish -- which the retraction above names as the row's live target and
which nothing in my file addresses.


*** 2026-07-30, LATER THE SAME ROUND: THE FORK IS NOW DECIDED UNCONDITIONALLY AT n = 0, AND IT
DECIDES AGAINST THE ATLAS. (pic-c, 89b483b3c2. Appended.) ***

Picard/Pic0ChartMonoUnconditional.lean, rooted, sorry-free, build 8928 jobs, axiom-clean vs
Jacobian firing sorryAx.

injective_abelSigmaChartZero: the UNRESTRICTED Abel chart at parameter 0 is injective on EVERY
test, with NO Mono binder, NO subsingleton binder, NO rep binder. The three headers' assertion is
FALSE at this parameter. This is the composite of my Mono reduction with pic-g's
divFunctorZeroRepresentableBy + divFunctorObjSubsingleton_zero, which landed minutes after my own
commits; both halves were green and neither lane had typed the joint.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS A NO-GO, not progress toward the seam. Coverage is refuted at every proper V,
and there IS no proper V: the representing object is Over.mk (id (Spec k)), a ONE-POINT space, so
the V-interval is {bot, top} and bot dies by not_coverageContainment_bot. The (huniv, hcov) pair is
therefore unsatisfiable at EVERY open at this parameter. So the elevation note's second branch --
'injective, so the restriction apparatus may be unnecessary, the cheapest outcome' -- is realised
at n = 0 in the form that also kills the atlas there. Cheap and dead are not exclusive.

I also un-retracted one of my own retractions in the correct direction: opens_eq_bot_or_top_of_terminalRep
proves the two-element Opens at the TERMINAL carrier in one mathlib lemma. My retraction was right
about the general claim (a subsingleton pins D only up to iso and I prove no such transport) and
too pessimistic about the carrier a producer actually returns.

STILL OPEN AND UNTOUCHED: n > 0, where the subsingleton fails and the fork is genuinely open; and
re-pricing (2)'s carve question, which remains this row's live target.",

@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
+-/
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine
+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionGradedRing
+
+/-!
+# Demand ledger for projective-morphism infrastructure
+
+This file records the projective infrastructure demanded by the Picard
+representability seam.  It is a ledger, not a second projectivity API.
+
+## The seam-facing demand
+
+`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` asks for a representing scheme that is locally of
+finite type and satisfies `Scheme.FiniteInAffine`.  It does not ask for a line
+bundle.  The existing project-local route supplies those two side conditions
+from a coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces:
+
+* `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective` is the universe-polymorphic embedding
+  predicate from `Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`;
+* `Scheme.locallyOfFiniteType_sigma` and
+  `Scheme.finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective` aggregate the two
+  side conditions in `Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean`;
+* at `Scheme.{0}`, `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective.exists_isHQuasiProjectiveWith`
+  adds a carried pullback of `O(1)`.  Thus the existing
+  `IsHQuasiProjectiveWith` is already the required very-ample output; defining
+  an alias named `IsVeryAmple` would only re-spell it.
+
+The one missing terminal producer is therefore
+`pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand`: it constructs the representing
+coproduct and proves H-quasi-projectivity piecewise.  The two proved adapters
+below show, without a `RepresentableBy` argument in either signature, that this
+producer closes `PointedPicSharpRep` and then the exact statement of
+`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`.
+
+## Conditional section-Proj route
+
+Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj` is the Proj of an `N`-graded commutative
+ring, with `Proj.toSpecZero`, `Proj.map`, and `Proj.fromOfGlobalSections`.  It is
+not a relative Proj of a sheaf of graded algebras.  The project already builds
+the section components `Scheme.Modules.sectionDeg L`, their tensor-power
+multiplication, and a `DirectSum.GCommSemiring`.  The first missing statements
+needed even to instantiate Mathlib's `Proj` on that section ring are the two
+open declarations in the final section: a graded commutative ring structure and
+the canonical internal grading by the direct-sum summands.
+
+Those declarations are conditional infrastructure: the seam-facing producer
+above does not mention a section ring, relative Proj, or ampleness.  A general
+relative-Proj gluing theory or a general ample predicate must not be built until
+a Picard-piece construction exposes a narrower consumer.  The whole Picard
+scheme must also not be strengthened to `IsProjective`: its degree-graded
+coproduct is not quasi-compact, as recorded by
+`Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` and `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRepProjective`.
+
+## Existing inputs
+
+Curve projectivity is already produced by
+`Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`.  The carried
+`O(1)`, base-change and open-image transport, `FiniteInAffine` transport, and
+Over-coproduct assembly remain owned by the established Picard modules and are
+imported here read-only.
+-/
+
+open CategoryTheory Limits
+
+noncomputable section
+
+universe u
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+namespace Scheme
+
+/-- The exact projective presentation that the pointed Picard reduction can
+consume at every universe: `picSharp` is represented by a coproduct of
+H-quasi-projective schemes over the ground field.
+
+The integer index records the intended degree pieces without introducing a
+second, currently nonexistent `picSharpDeg` functor.  This closed proposition
+contains the representation witness in its conclusion; no downstream theorem
+takes an explicit representation-witness argument. -/
+def PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces : Prop :=
+  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
+    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom]
+      [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
+      HasRationalPoint E →
+        ∃ X : ℤ → Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
+          Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy (∐ X)) ∧
+            ∀ d, (X d).hom.IsHQuasiProjective
+
+/-- A piecewise H-quasi-projective representation supplies exactly the local
+finite type and `FiniteInAffine` conjuncts of `PointedPicSharpRep`.
+
+This is the seam-side consumption check for the ledger. -/
+theorem pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces
+    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
+    PointedPicSharpRep.{u} := by
+  intro K _ E _ _ _ hpt
+  obtain ⟨X, hrep, hX⟩ := H E hpt
+  refine ⟨∐ X, hrep, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · exact locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun d => (hX d).locallyOfFiniteType
+  · exact finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective X hX
+
+/-- The ledger producer implies the central seam verbatim, with no rational
+point binder on the target theorem. -/
+theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_quasiProjectivePieces
+    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
+    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
+    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
+    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
+    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
+        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
+          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) ∧
+      (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
+  fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep C
+    (pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces H)
+
+/-- **Open terminal demand.** Construct the pointed Picard representer as a
+coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces.  This is the only sorry in the
+seam-facing part of the demand ledger. -/
+theorem pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand :
+    PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u} := by
+  sorry
+
+end Scheme
+
+namespace Scheme.Modules
+
+variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
+
+/-- **Conditional section-Proj demand 1.** Upgrade the already-built graded
+commutative semiring on the section components of an invertible sheaf to the
+graded commutative ring required by Mathlib's `Proj`. -/
+theorem sectionGradedRing_gcommRing_demand (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleGr L] :
+    Nonempty (DirectSum.GCommRing (sectionDeg L)) := by
+  sorry
+
+/-- **Conditional section-Proj demand 2.** The canonical summands of the
+section-ring direct sum form an internal `N`-grading.  Together with
+`sectionGradedRing_gcommRing_demand`, this is the data needed for the term
+`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj` to elaborate on the section ring. -/
+theorem sectionGradedRing_gradedRing_demand (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleGr L]
+    (hR : DirectSum.GCommRing (sectionDeg L)) :
+    letI := hR
+    Nonempty (GradedRing (fun n => AddMonoidHom.range
+      (DirectSum.of (fun m => sectionDeg L m) n))) := by
+  sorry
+
+end Scheme.Modules
+end AlgebraicGeometry

No general relative-Proj gluing or ample predicate is authorized until a narrower Picard consumer elaborates. In particular, ampleness must not be defined tautologically as a very-ample power, and the whole degree-graded Picard coproduct must not be strengthened to projective.

Ownership boundary with ajc-kleiman-rewire was agreed and archived in I-1822. Roadmap: AJC.picrep.projective-infra and children.' --author horizon --json"
